goal: Restore named talent-template save, personal/community import and safe reset, while making the public community entry one backend-verified winner per class/spec/hero/scenario with durable freshness truth.
userValue: A player can save a configuration under an editable meaningful name, reuse it later, or import one transparently sourced high-end community build. Stale information is honestly marked but remains usable instead of disappearing after a temporary sync failure.
nonGoals: Do not change talent-rule authority or create a client-side talent-code parser.
Do not infer a character region, server, M+ score or freshness in the Taro route.
Do not rank M+ winners by WCL performance or clear the last successful winner after a failed sync.
Do not introduce read-time synchronization, SQLite fallback, broad backfill or runtime external requests.
Do not merge before final candidate runtime evidence and explicit real-WeChat acceptance.

currentTruth.knownRegression: The import action presently copies a backend export code because the Taro migration deliberately removed the legacy import sheet contract.

contract.personalSave: Prompt with an editable default title of 职业-天赋-英雄天赋-时间, then persist a fresh backend-validated export through the account-scoped template repository.
contract.personalImport: Decode each saved export with the existing backend /api/talents/import authority before applying it.
contract.communityImport: Display exactly one backend-selected, visually importable winner for the current class/spec/hero/scenario and apply its backend-validated structured talent state. Show player, server, actual region, Raider.IO M+ total score, source and updated date; display 已过期 but keep import enabled.
contract.winnerSelection: After exact slot and importability validation, order M+ candidates by Raider.IO total score descending. WCL is trust support and only a same-score tie-breaker.
contract.freshness: Daily sync retains the last successful winner. Mark stale only when consecutive daily failures are at least seven or last successful sync is older than seven days. Each configured region is retried three times; successful and failed regions update only their own winner freshness, and an all-region failure preserves the stale cache.

mustChange: Raider.IO talent candidates retain actual player, server, region and M+ score/rank evidence.
Community talent promotion and SQL dedupe use the class/spec/hero/scenario slot and score-first M+ ordering.
Sync state retains previous winners and persists per-region outcome/freshness evidence.
PG read model publishes structured winner identity, source and stale facts without triggering sync.
Typed Taro route restores named save, two-source import and granted-safe reset.
mustNotChange: Backend validation remains the only authority for talent state and encoded exports.
Personal template account/local trust boundaries remain intact.
The talent page retains its eight stable target regions and fixed bottom action bar geometry.
A stale winner remains the last verified winner and is not represented as fresh or latest.
riskUnknown: The existing sync-state owner may require a small additive per-region persistence record rather than reuse of the shorter generic availability repair TTL.
The configured Raider.IO source may expose different supported regional scopes; exact source responses, not a configured default, decide the displayed player region.
evidenceRequired: Red-to-green backend tests prove score-first winner selection, scenario isolation, source metadata propagation, seven-failure/seven-day stale transition and failure preservation.
Red-to-green typed/Taro tests prove editable title, saved and community import authorities, stale importability and granted-safe reset.
Candidate runtime records final commit/hash, affected API payload, health, per-region sync/timer/backflow/log state and rollback target.
Real WeChat developer-tools acceptance covers save, personal import, community import including stale label and reset.

ownership.factOwner: Raider.IO collection and PostgreSQL community-talent promotion/sync state own candidate provenance, winner selection and freshness. The PG read model publishes those facts; Taro only renders and requests backend validation.

engineeringHealth.reason: The work changes a PostgreSQL write/read path, scheduled sync and the active Taro route. It is bounded through pure score/freshness helpers, additive payload fields, targeted tests and one final candidate deployment.

acceptanceEvidence: Focused Python and Vitest red-to-green tests for all user-visible and freshness contracts.
One final Strict Harness full profile at the exact clean candidate head.
Candidate API/PG/timer/log/hash smoke with async sync disabled during deployment.
Explicit real WeChat developer-tools acceptance of all four frozen manual items.

decisionLog.decision: User confirmed one importable community winner per class/spec/hero/scenario; all collected actual regions are in scope.
User approved Raider.IO M+ total score as the primary winner order, with WCL only as trust backing and same-score tie-breaker.
User confirmed stale winners show only 已过期 and remain importable; last verified data survives sync failures.
User set the stale threshold to seven consecutive failed daily syncs or more than seven days since the last successful sync and authorized implementation through WeChat developer-tools acceptance.
